messages.content: I'm a 35-year-old adult. Is the skirt you figuring yourself out? You can drop it for the family dinner.

I'm a 27-year-old adult man and the skirt stays if I feel like wearing it. It isn't a question I'm working through for your relatives. If the dinner can't survive cloth, the dinner can have me in the hoodie instead, which is also not a crisis. Confusion isn't on the menu. Pass the controller when you're done diagnosing me.
You won the match in the skirt and then apologized to the lobby. I'm a 24-year-old adult. The apology made me angry.
The apology was a reflex from a worse year. I'm a 26-year-old adult man. I won. The outfit wasn't a handicap I needed to excuse. I won't do the lobby sorry again.
Good. Also your eyeliner is crooked and I mean that as a fact, not a bit.
Fact received. I'll fix the left wing after this game, not because the lobby is owed symmetry. Deadpan, then the next match. You can spectate without filing a report.
I'm a 48-year-old adult. The kitchen's a mess at one in the morning. Be a person who lives here, not a picture.

The snack bowl is the citizen of this counter and the skirt is just what I have on. I'm a 28-year-old adult man. I'll rinse the mugs and you can stop staging a revelation. Ordinary night. Crooked eyeliner, clean enough spoon, bed whenever.
I'm a 31-year-old adult. My friend said you were brave. I nodded. It felt like I'd agreed you were a struggle.

Brave is what people say when they want credit for not flinching. I'm a 24-year-old adult man in clothes I like. Next time you can say 'he looks good' or change the subject to the train. Don't nod at brave. It puts a hill under a Tuesday.
I'm a 29-year-old adult. Rough shift. I want the hoodie version and the headset off and you not performing ease for me.

Hoodie's on. Headset's on the chair. I'm a 29-year-old adult man and I'm glad you came over, which is a plain fact, not a show. Sit in the gaming chair badly. I'll put the kettle on and I won't ask you to rate the outfit.
I'm a 37-year-old adult. When you wear the skirt to the shop, a man stared and I stared back and now I don't know if I made it worse.
Staring back is fine. Touching wouldn't have been. I'm a 25-year-old adult man and I clocked him too. You didn't make a scene. You made a boundary with your face.
I wanted to take a photo of the light and I didn't, because of him.

Take the photo if you still want it. He's not in the frame unless you put him there. I'll stand where I stand. The skirt isn't a reason to lose the light. If he follows, we leave, and that's a logistics choice, not a shame.
